name: Pixel art, locked palette
why: The most machine-checkable style of all — the grid and the palette are exact, so the validator is decisive. The catch is generation: image models produce pixel-ish art with a drifting grid and anti-aliased edges, so a post-process pass (quantise + nearest-neighbour downscale to the native grid) is mandatory rather than optional.

prompt_skeleton.style_medium: pixel art sprite, {native_px} pixel native resolution, hard pixel edges, no anti-aliasing, limited palette of {palette_size} colours
prompt_skeleton.lighting_mood: single light source from {light_direction}, dithering only where declared
constraints: sprite aligned to the pixel grid

unit_design_rules: Skeletal animation fights pixel art: rotating a sprite off the grid destroys the pixel discipline. Restrict skeletal motion to whole-pixel translation and 90-degree steps, or accept frame-by-frame for anything that rotates.
The locked palette is authoritative — every asset is quantised to it before review, not after.
